qualifying_findings.title: n8n MCP OAuth dynamic-client registration open redirect
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Public GitHub Advisory Database record corroborated by an n8n repository advisory and NVD reference.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: n8n before 1.123.89; 2.x before 2.45.5; 2.46.x before 2.46.1; and 3.x before 3.0.1. The exposed boundary is the unauthenticated /mcp-oauth/register dynamic-client-registration endpoint.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-126386 states that arbitrary redirect_uri values were accepted during unauthenticated MCP OAuth client registration. Crafted authorization URLs could redirect a visitor to an attacker-controlled site before instance checks, enabling phishing.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Remote MCP authorization is a delegated-authority boundary. An open redirect at registration/authorization can undermine user trust in agent-to-tool consent flows even when the underlying workflow platform is otherwise authenticated.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: n8n as a general workflow/MCP product belongs to ai-wiki; the security-specific OAuth boundary and patch implication remain locally owned.

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise Custom Function sandbox SSRF bypass
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Public GitHub Advisory Database record with reproducible public researcher technical evidence; no maintainer-authored remediation was identified in the advisory record.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flowise through 3.1.4. An authenticated actor with chatflow or agentflow create/update permission can reach POST /api/v1/node-custom-function and import a subpath of an allowlisted HTTP package to bypass Custom Function SSRF checks.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-127214 reports that package subpath imports such as axios/dist/node/axios.cjs evade the vm2 mock table and return an HTTP client that skips checkDenyList validation. The advisory describes arbitrary GET and POST requests to loopback, internal-network, or cloud-metadata addresses, enabling mapping, credential disclosure, and internal-service state changes.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agentflow editing permission becomes an internal-network and cloud-credential boundary when agent custom functions can bypass SSRF controls. This is relevant to least privilege, runtime isolation, and tool execution assurance.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Flowise product context belongs to ai-wiki; general agent-workflow development practice belongs to ai-dev-wiki. Retain only the local security finding, permission boundary, and remediation-verification note.

qualifying_findings.title: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway Web UI DOM XSS fixed in v1.1.0
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary IBM security bulletin, corroborated by the public GitHub Advisory Database record.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway v1.0.0 through v1.0.11; IBM identifies v1.1.0 as the remediation release. The boundary is administrator-facing dashboard notification rendering from page-URL values.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: IBM says a mutation-XSS sanitizer bypass in dashboard status/error notifications can allow arbitrary JavaScript in an administrator's authenticated session when the administrator opens a crafted link. IBM rates CVE-2026-110199 CVSS 4.8 and recommends upgrading to v1.1.0; it states no workaround.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP gateway administration plane can hold routing and credential-control authority. Script execution in an authenticated administrator session can expose trusted-session credentials or alter gateway behavior.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ContextForge is an upstream-owned MCP product entity in ai-wiki; preserve the security-specific administration-plane and fixed-version evidence in this security wiki.
